questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Retail trading can take place without a fixed shop, through street peddling, handcarts, door-to-door sales, mail order and the internet.
Reason (R): Retail trading is the business of selling goods directly to consumers.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true — NCERT defines retail trading as the sale of goods directly to consumers and lists these non-store forms. But the definition of retail trade does not explain why it can take place without a store; it is true of store retail too.
Why not the others: (A) treats the definition as the cause; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: Most retail trading still takes place in fixed establishments or stores.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: Mumbai High, India's important offshore oilfield in the Arabian Sea, was discovered in which year?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 1973
Why: NCERT notes that oil was struck at Mumbai High in 1973 and production started in 1976.
Why not the others: 1959 (A) is linked with oil finds in Gujarat; 1984 (B) is the year GAIL was set up; 1991 (C) is the year of economic reforms.
Key point: Mumbai High lies about 160 km off Mumbai.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Bilateral trade
(B) Multilateral trade
(C) Free trade
(D) Dumping

List-II
(I) Selling a commodity in another country at a price unrelated to its cost
(II) Opening up economies by removing barriers such as tariffs
(III) Trade with many countries; a country may give "Most Favoured Nation" status to some partners
(IV) Trade between two countries under an agreement between them
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: bilateral trade is between two countries under an agreement (IV); multilateral trade is with many countries, sometimes with MFN status (III); free trade means removing trade barriers (II); dumping is selling at prices unrelated to costs (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps bilateral and multilateral trade; (B) swaps multilateral and free trade; (D) swaps free trade and dumping.
Key point: The WTO sets the rules for multilateral trade.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: In some advanced regions, livestock — especially poultry and cattle — are reared in stalls and pens, fed on manufactured feedstuff and carefully supervised against diseases. This is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Factory farming
Why: NCERT calls this factory farming, a form of modern livestock rearing practised in Western Europe and North America.
Why not the others: Mixed farming (A) combines crops and livestock; truck farming (C) grows vegetables; ranching (D) rears animals on large open pastures.
Key point: Factory farming needs heavy capital investment in buildings, machinery and veterinary services.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: Why did India adopt regional (area-specific) planning in addition to sectoral planning?
options: A) Because sectoral planning is not allowed under the Constitution
B) Because every region of India had developed equally by 1950
C) Because development has not been uniform, and some regions lag behind others
D) Because planning should be done only by the states, not by the Centre
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Because development has not been uniform, and some regions lag behind others
Why: NCERT notes that the economic development of a country is not uniform over space; some areas are more developed and others lag behind, so an area-specific approach is needed to reduce regional imbalances.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are incorrect statements.
Key point: Target-area programmes are a form of regional planning.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about environmental pollution:
(A) Industries, agriculture and domestic sewage are sources of water pollution.
(B) Noise pollution is spread evenly over a city, whatever the distance from its source.
(C) Air pollution harms the respiratory, nervous and circulatory systems.
(D) Land pollution is caused only by natural processes and never by people.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A) and (C) only
Why: (A) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (B) is false — noise pollution is location-specific; its intensity falls with distance. (D) is false — land pollution is caused largely by human activities such as dumping of waste. Every other option includes (B) or (D).
Key point: Pollution is the release of substances or energy that harm the environment.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: What is rainwater harvesting?
options: A) Pumping groundwater to the surface for irrigation
B) Capturing and storing rainwater for various uses
C) Building dams across large rivers to make power
D) Diverting river water through canals to dry areas
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Capturing and storing rainwater for various uses
Why: NCERT defines rainwater harvesting as a method to capture and store rainwater for various uses; it is also used to recharge groundwater aquifers.
Why not the others: (A) uses groundwater; (C) and (D) are large river projects, not rainwater harvesting.
Key point: Rainwater harvesting is a low-cost and eco-friendly technique.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: India's population was about 102.9 crore in 2001 and about 121.1 crore in 2011. What was the decadal growth rate, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 17.7 per cent
Given: 2001 = 102.9 crore; 2011 = 121.1 crore.
Step 1: Increase = 121.1 − 102.9 = 18.2 crore.
Step 2: Growth rate = 18.2 ÷ 102.9 × 100 ≈ 17.7 per cent.
Common mistake: giving the increase in crore as the rate (18.2, option C), or dividing by the 2011 figure (about 15.0 per cent, option A).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question: According to NCERT, which group of items accounts for the largest share of India's imports?
options: A) Petroleum, crude and its products
B) Food grains, pulses and edible oils
D) Iron ore, manganese and mica
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Petroleum, crude and its products
Why: NCERT notes that petroleum, crude and products make up the largest share of India's imports.
Why not the others: Food grains (B) were large imports only in the 1950s–60s; tea, coffee (C), iron ore and manganese (D) are exports.
Key point: Imports of fertilisers, machinery and gems are also important.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: In extensive commercial grain cultivation, farms are very large and almost every operation is mechanised. What is NCERT's description of its yields?
options: A) Low yield per acre but high yield per person
B) High yield per acre and high yield per person
C) High yield per acre but low yield per person
D) Low yield per acre and low yield per person
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Low yield per acre but high yield per person
Why: NCERT notes that in extensive commercial grain cultivation the yield per acre is low, but the yield per person is high, because few people farm very large areas with machines.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) describe intensive farming patterns; (D) describes neither.
Key point: Wheat is the principal crop, with maize, barley, oats and rye.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about population growth:
(A) Natural growth of population includes the effect of migration.
(B) Actual growth = births − deaths + in-migration − out-migration.
(C) Positive growth of population occurs when the birth rate is higher than the death rate, or when people migrate in permanently.
(D) The crude birth rate is expressed as the number of live births in a year per thousand of population.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (C) and (D) only
Why: (B), (C) and (D) follow NCERT's definitions.
Why not the others: (A) is false — natural growth is only births minus deaths; migration is added to give actual growth. Every other option includes (A).
Key point: Natural growth + net migration = actual growth.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: According to NCERT, crude petroleum in India occurs in:
options: A) old crystalline rocks of the peninsular plateau
B) igneous rocks of the Deccan traps
C) metamorphic rocks of the Dharwar system
D) sedimentary rocks of the tertiary period
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) sedimentary rocks of the tertiary period
Why: NCERT states that crude petroleum occurs in sedimentary rocks of the tertiary period.
Why not the others: Metallic minerals occur in old crystalline rocks (A); the Deccan traps (B) are basaltic; the Dharwar rocks (C) carry copper and zinc in the north-west.
Key point: Oil exploration in India began in 1956 with the Oil and Natural Gas Commission.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question: In NCERT's description of the Human Development Index, access to knowledge is represented by:
options: A) the number of universities and colleges per lakh people
B) the adult literacy rate and the gross enrolment ratio
C) the share of the budget spent on education
D) the number of teachers per school
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) the adult literacy rate and the gross enrolment ratio
Why: NCERT notes that the adult literacy rate and the gross enrolment ratio represent access to knowledge, one of the three dimensions of the HDI.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are inputs to education, not the indicators NCERT names.
Key point: The other two dimensions are a long and healthy life and access to resources.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question: Which approach to human development looks at human beings as beneficiaries or targets of development activities, and argues for higher government spending on education, health and social amenities?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The welfare approach
Why: NCERT describes the welfare approach in these words; it holds that development will come from maximising government spending on welfare.
Why not the others: The income approach (A) links development with income; the basic needs approach (B) focuses on six needs; the capability approach (C) builds human capabilities, as Amartya Sen argued.
Key point: In the welfare approach people are not participants in development, only passive recipients.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question: In transport geography, distance can be measured in three ways. They are:
options: B) straight-line, curved and spiral distance
C) local, regional and global distance
D) km distance, time distance and cost distance
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) km distance, time distance and cost distance
Why: NCERT notes that distance can be measured as km distance (route length), time distance (time taken to travel) and cost distance (the expense of travelling on a route).
Why not the others: (A) gives position, not distance; (B) and (C) are not NCERT's measures.
Key point: Transport planners choose routes to minimise cost or time.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question: The deep ravines of the Chambal valley are an example of which kind of degraded land, according to NCERT's classification?
options: A) Land degraded by mining and industrial waste dumps
B) Natural degradation in the form of gullies and ravines
C) Land degraded by waterlogging in canal command areas
D) Land degraded by repeated shifting cultivation
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Natural degradation in the form of gullies and ravines
Why: NCERT classes gullied and ravinous land as land degraded by natural processes; the Chambal ravines are the classic example.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are kinds of land degraded by human action.
Key point: Gully erosion is a serious problem in the Chambal basin of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: How does modern agriculture add to water pollution, according to NCERT?
options: A) Fertilisers and pesticides seep into groundwater and rivers
B) Crops absorb all the water, so that rivers and lakes run dry
C) Farm machinery releases large amounts of oil into the sea
D) Harvesting removes all the dissolved minerals from the water
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Fertilisers and pesticides seep into groundwater and rivers
Why: NCERT notes that the use of chemical fertilisers, insecticides and pesticides in agriculture pollutes surface water and groundwater.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not NCERT's explanation.
Key point: Industrial effluents and urban sewage are the other major sources of water pollution.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: Services cannot be measured in tonnes. So, according to NCERT, the volume of a country's trade is taken to be:
options: A) the total weight of goods exported and imported
B) the total value of goods and services traded
C) the difference between exports and imports
D) the number of ships entering its ports
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) the total value of goods and services traded
Why: NCERT explains that the actual tonnage of goods makes up the volume, but since services cannot be weighed, the total value of goods and services traded is taken as the volume of trade.
Why not the others: (A) leaves out services; (C) is the balance of trade; (D) is not a measure of trade volume.
Key point: Trade is also described by its composition and direction.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: Density of population is the number of persons per unit area. A region of 40,000 square kilometres has a density of 250 persons per square kilometre. What is its population?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 1 crore
Given: density = 250 persons per sq km; area = 40,000 sq km.
Step 1: Population = density × area.
Step 2: 250 × 40,000 = 1,00,00,000 = 1 crore.
Common mistake: dividing area by density (160, wrongly read as 16 lakh, option A), or dropping zeros (10 lakh, option C).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question: Mathura, Amritsar, Madurai and Puri are grouped together in NCERT's functional classification of towns. To which class do they belong?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Religious and cultural towns
Why: NCERT lists Varanasi, Mathura, Amritsar, Madurai, Puri, Ajmer, Pushkar, Tirupati, Kurukshetra, Haridwar and Ujjain as religious and cultural towns.
Why not the others: Educational towns (A) include Roorkee, Aligarh and Pilani; transport towns (C) include Kandla, Itarsi and Katni; tourist towns (D) include Nainital, Mussoorie and Mount Abu.
Key point: Varanasi is both an ancient town and a religious and cultural town.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: Wheat is the second most important cereal of India. Which description matches NCERT?
options: A) It is mainly a kharif crop of the humid eastern states
B) It is grown mostly in the wet coastal plains of Kerala and Odisha
C) It needs over 200 cm of rainfall and standing water
D) It is mainly a rabi crop, concentrated in the north and central regions
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) It is mainly a rabi crop, concentrated in the north and central regions
Why: NCERT notes that wheat is mainly a rabi (winter) crop and that about 85 per cent of its area is in the north and central regions — the Indo-Gangetic plain, the Malwa plateau and the Himalayas up to 2,700 m.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) describe the conditions of rice, not wheat.
Key point: Wheat is grown in irrigated and rainfed conditions in the cool season.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question:
Arrange the following towns in the order in which they first developed, from the earliest to the latest:
(A) Chandigarh
(B) Agra
(C) Pataliputra
(D) Mumbai
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (C), (B), (D), (A)
Why: Pataliputra is an ancient town (C); Agra developed in the medieval period (B); Mumbai was developed by the British (D); Chandigarh was planned after Independence (A).
Why not the others: (B) puts Agra before Pataliputra; (C) puts Mumbai before Agra; (D) puts Chandigarh before Mumbai.
Key point: NCERT groups towns as ancient, medieval and modern.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: India grows mostly a superior quality of coffee that is in great demand in the international market. Which variety is it?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Arabica
Why: NCERT notes that there are three varieties — arabica, robusta and liberica — and that India mostly grows arabica.
Why not the others: Robusta (A) and liberica (B) are the other two varieties NCERT names; excelsa (D) is not mentioned.
Key point: Karnataka produces more than two-thirds of India's coffee.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question:
Arrange the following figures for India's water resources in descending order of volume:
(A) Usable surface water
(B) Total utilisable water resource
(C) Mean annual flow of all river basins
(D) Replenishable groundwater
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (B), (A), (D)
Why: NCERT: the mean annual river flow is about 1,869 cubic km (C); the total utilisable water resource is about 1,122 cubic km (B); usable surface water is about 690 cubic km (A); replenishable groundwater is about 432 cubic km (D). Note that 690 + 432 = 1,122.
Why not the others: (A) puts usable surface water above the total; (B) puts the total above the river flow; (D) puts groundwater above surface water.
Key point: Only a part of the river flow can be used, because of topographical and hydrological constraints.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.sub_topic: Fields and sub-fields of human geography
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Sub-field)
(A) Electoral geography
(B) Tourism geography
(C) Gender geography
(D) Rural settlement geography

List-II (Field of human geography)
(I) Social geography
(II) Political geography
(III) Settlement geography
(IV) Economic geography
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: NCERT's table places electoral geography under political geography (II), tourism geography under economic geography (IV), gender geography under social geography (I), and rural settlement geography under settlement geography (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps electoral and tourism geography; (C) swaps tourism and gender geography; (D) swaps gender and rural settlement geography.
Key point: Economic geography also includes resource, agricultural, industrial, marketing and international trade geography.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Human Poverty Index:
(A) It measures the attainment of human development, just as the HDI does.
(B) It is a non-income measure.
(C) It considers the probability of not surviving to the age of 40, the adult illiteracy rate and access to clean water.
(D) It is another name for Gross National Happiness.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B) and (C) only
Why: (B) and (C) follow NCERT — the Human Poverty Index is a non-income measure that uses the probability of not surviving to 40, adult illiteracy, lack of clean water and the number of underweight small children.
Why not the others: (A) is false — it measures the shortfall in human development, not attainment. (D) is false — Gross National Happiness is Bhutan's measure. Every other option includes (A) or (D).
Key point: Looking at both indices gives a more accurate picture of human development.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.sub_topic: Major ports of the west coast
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about ports of India:
(A) Kandla (Deendayal) is a tidal port developed after Partition.
(B) Mumbai is a natural harbour and the biggest port of the country.
(C) Kochi is an artificial harbour located in Karnataka.
(D) Paradip is located in the Godavari delta of Andhra Pradesh.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A) and (B) only
Why: (A) and (B) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (C) is false — Kochi is a natural harbour at the head of the Vembanad Kayal in Kerala. (D) is false — Paradip is in the Mahanadi delta in Odisha. Every other option includes (C) or (D).
Key point: Mumbai's hinterland covers Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and parts of other states.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Place)
(A) Kaiga
(B) Manikaran
(C) Okhla
(D) Digboi

List-II (Energy feature)
(I) A field-based oil refinery
(II) A plant producing energy from municipal waste
(III) A geothermal energy plant
(IV) A nuclear power station
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Kaiga in Karnataka has a nuclear power station (IV); Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh has a geothermal plant (III); Okhla in Delhi turns municipal waste into energy (II); Digboi in Assam has a field-based refinery (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps Kaiga and Manikaran; (C) swaps Manikaran and Okhla; (D) swaps Okhla and Digboi.
Key point: Nuclear, geothermal and bio-energy all reduce dependence on coal.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Read the following statements on India's highway projects:
(A) The National Highways Authority of India was made operational in 1995.
(B) The Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.
(C) The East–West Corridor links Silchar in Assam with Porbandar in Gujarat.
(D) The North–South Corridor links Delhi with Kolkata.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — the North–South Corridor links Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir with Kanniyakumari in Tamil Nadu. Options (B) and (C) include (D); option (D) leaves out the true statement (B).
Key point: NHAI implements these highway projects.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Rice in Punjab and Haryana is grown mainly without irrigation, using monsoon rain alone.
Reason (R): Punjab and Haryana receive fairly low rainfall but have extensive canal and tube-well irrigation.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
Why: The Reason is true. The Assertion is false — Punjab and Haryana are not traditional rice areas; NCERT notes that rice was introduced in their irrigated areas in the 1970s, after the Green Revolution.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) need a true Assertion.
Key point: Rice there is a commercial crop that draws heavily on groundwater.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: In India, groups such as the Gujjars, Bakarwals, Gaddis and Bhotiyas move from the plains to the mountains in summer and back to the plains in winter with their herds. This seasonal movement is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Transhumance
Why: NCERT calls the seasonal migration of herders between plains and mountains transhumance, and names these groups as examples.
Why not the others: Shifting cultivation (A) is a farming system; ranching (B) is commercial and sedentary; reindeer herding (C) is in the Arctic.
Key point: In mountains, herders move up in summer and down in winter.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: Which of the following does NCERT list among the measures that can help population control?
options: A) Raising the retirement age and cutting old-age pensions for all
B) Banning migration from rural areas to cities
C) Free contraceptives and tax disincentives for large families
D) Reducing the number of schools in rural areas
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Free contraceptives and tax disincentives for large families
Why: NCERT notes that propaganda, the free availability of contraceptives and tax disincentives for large families can help population control; access to family planning services is a significant factor.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not NCERT's measures, and fewer schools would work against lower fertility.
Key point: Family planning means the spacing or preventing of births.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question:
In modern times some gathering has become commercial. Match each part of a plant with its uses, as described by NCERT.

List-I (Part of plant)
(A) Bark
(B) Leaves
(C) Nuts
(D) Tree trunks

List-II (Uses)
(I) Food and oils
(II) Rubber, balata, gums and resins
(III) Quinine, tannin extract and cork
(IV) Beverages, drugs, cosmetics, fibres and thatch
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: NCERT: bark is used for quinine, tannin extract and cork (III); leaves supply materials for beverages, drugs, cosmetics, fibres and thatch (IV); nuts give food and oils (I); tree trunks yield rubber, balata, gums and resins (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps leaves and nuts; (B) swaps bark and leaves; (D) swaps nuts and tree trunks.
Key point: Gathering has little chance of becoming important globally, as synthetic products replace many forest products.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, Muslims, the largest religious minority in India, are concentrated in which group of areas?
options: A) J&K, parts of West Bengal and Kerala, UP, Delhi and Lakshadweep
B) Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, with smaller numbers in Rajasthan
C) Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and the Chotanagpur region
D) Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Tripura and Lahul and Spiti
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) J&K, parts of West Bengal and Kerala, UP, Delhi and Lakshadweep
Why: NCERT notes that Muslims are concentrated in Jammu and Kashmir, certain districts of West Bengal and Kerala, many districts of Uttar Pradesh, in and around Delhi, and in Lakshadweep.
Why not the others: (B) is where Sikhs are concentrated; (C) is where Christians are concentrated; (D) is where Buddhists are found in large numbers.
Key point: Lakshadweep has a Muslim majority.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: Which state is the leading producer of manganese in India, with major mines at Bonai, Kendujhar and Sundergarh?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Odisha
Why: NCERT notes that Odisha is the leading producer of manganese; its major mines are in the central part of the iron ore belt, at Bonai, Kendujhar, Sundergarh, Gangpur, Koraput, Kalahandi and Bolangir.
Why not the others: Karnataka (A), Madhya Pradesh (B, with Balaghat) and Maharashtra (D, with Nagpur and Bhandara) also produce manganese, but less than Odisha.
Key point: Manganese is an important raw material for smelting iron ore.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: According to NCERT, India's coastline, including its islands, is about how long?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 7,517 km
Why: NCERT notes that India has a long coastline of about 7,517 km, including its islands, which supports 12 major and about 200 minor ports.
Why not the others: 15,200 km (B) is roughly the length of India's land border; (A) and (C) are not NCERT's figures.
Key point: Ocean shipping carries most of India's foreign trade by volume.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: Which national television channel of India is one of the largest terrestrial networks in the world?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Doordarshan
Why: NCERT notes that Doordarshan, the national television channel of India, is one of the largest terrestrial networks in the world.
Why not the others: Akashvani (A) is All India Radio; (C) and (D) are not national television channels.
Key point: Television and radio are means of mass communication.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: According to Census 2011, as given in NCERT, what was the average density of population of India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 382 persons per sq km
Why: NCERT gives India's density of population in 2011 as 382 persons per sq km.
Why not the others: 117 (A) was the density in 1951; 1,102 (B) is the figure for Bihar; 17 (D) is the figure for Arunachal Pradesh.
Key point: Density has risen more than three times since 1951.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: Which body replaced the Planning Commission of India on 1 January 2015?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) NITI Aayog
Why: NCERT notes that the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) on 1 January 2015.
Why not the others: The National Development Council (B), the Finance Commission (C) and the Inter-State Council (D) are other bodies with different roles.
Key point: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach and involves the states in planning.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: How has the role of labour as a factor in the location of industry changed in the 21st century, according to NCERT?
options: A) Industries now locate only where unskilled labour is the cheapest in the world
B) Labour has become the single most important factor in industrial location
C) Mechanisation and automation have reduced industry's dependence on labour
D) Labour no longer matters at all for any kind of industry today
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Mechanisation and automation have reduced industry's dependence on labour
Why: NCERT notes that increasing mechanisation, automation and flexibility of industrial processes have reduced the dependence of industry on the workforce, although some industries still need skilled labour.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) overstate the role of labour; (D) ignores the industries that still need skilled workers.
Key point: Markets, raw materials, energy and transport remain important location factors.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Human geography is highly interdisciplinary in nature.
Reason (R): It develops close links with sister disciplines of the social sciences in order to explain the relationship between people and space.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. NCERT explains that human geography tries to explain the relationship between all elements of human life and the space they occur over, so it develops a close interface with other social sciences — which is why it is interdisciplinary.
Why not the others: (B) would need an unrelated Reason; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: Sister disciplines include sociology, economics, political science, demography and history.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question:
Arrange the following in the order in which they happened, from the earliest to the latest:
(A) The start of agro-climatic planning by the Planning Commission
(B) The Intensive Agricultural District Programme
(C) The First Five Year Plan's focus on agriculture
(D) The Green Revolution with high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C), (B), (D), (A)
Why: The First Five Year Plan began in 1951 (C); IADP was launched in the early 1960s (B); the Green Revolution came in the mid-1960s (D); agro-climatic planning began in 1988 (A).
Why not the others: (A) puts IADP before the First Plan; (C) puts the Green Revolution before IADP; (D) puts agro-climatic planning before the Green Revolution.
Key point: Agro-climatic planning aimed at regionally balanced agricultural development.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: Why do governments often set up industries in particular areas, according to NCERT?
options: A) To keep all industries close to the national capital
B) Because industries cannot be set up by private companies
C) To avoid building roads and power lines elsewhere
D) To promote balanced development through regional policies
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) To promote balanced development through regional policies
Why: NCERT notes that governments adopt regional policies to promote balanced economic development, and therefore set up industries in particular areas.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not reasons NCERT gives; the private sector also sets up industries.
Key point: Government policy is one of the factors of industrial location.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.sub_topic: Use of the demographic transition theory
questions.question: According to NCERT, what can the demographic transition theory be used for?
options: A) To describe and predict the future population of any area
B) To measure the human development of a country in US dollars
C) To classify the occupations of a country's workers
D) To explain why industries locate near raw materials
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) To describe and predict the future population of any area
Why: NCERT says demographic transition theory can be used to describe and predict the future population of any area; it shows a change from high births and deaths to low births and deaths.
Why not the others: (B) is the HDI; (C) is occupational composition; (D) is a theme of industrial location.
Key point: Societies move from rural, agrarian and illiterate to urban, industrial and literate.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Category of worker)
(A) Cultivator
(B) Agricultural labourer
(C) Household industry worker
(D) Other workers

List-II (Description)
(I) Works in trade, transport, services or factories outside the household
(II) Makes goods at home, such as handloom cloth or pottery, within the household
(III) Works on another person's land for wages in money or kind
(IV) Works on land owned or taken on lease by himself or herself
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: A cultivator works his or her own or leased land (IV); an agricultural labourer works on another's land for wages (III); a household industry worker produces goods within the household (II); other workers include those in trade, transport, services and manufacturing outside the household (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps cultivators and labourers; (B) swaps labourers and household workers; (C) swaps household and other workers.
Key point: Cultivators and agricultural labourers together form the primary-sector workforce.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.sub_topic: Eastern terminal of the Trans-Siberian Railway
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Trans-continental railways run across a continent and link its two ends. They were built for economic and political reasons, to develop long runs in different directions.

The Trans-Siberian Railway is the most important rail route in Asia and the longest double-tracked and electrified trans-continental railway in the world, about 9,332 km long. It runs across Russia from the Baltic coast in the west to the Pacific coast in the east, passing through Moscow, Ufa, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk, Chita and Khabarovsk, and crosses the Ural mountains and the Ob and Yenisei rivers. It has helped to open up the Asian region to West European markets.

The Trans-Canadian Railway, about 7,050 km long, was built in 1886, initially as part of an agreement to bring British Columbia into the Canadian federation. It runs from the Atlantic coast to the Pacific coast, through Montreal, Ottawa, Winnipeg and Calgary, and links the Quebec–Montreal industrial region with the wheat belt of the Prairies and the coniferous forest region to the north.

Other trans-continental routes cross the USA, Australia and Europe.

Question: The Trans-Siberian Railway begins at St. Petersburg in the west. Which city on the Pacific coast is its eastern terminal?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Vladivostok
Why: NCERT notes that the Trans-Siberian Railway runs from St. Petersburg in the west to Vladivostok on the Pacific coast in the east.
Why not the others: Khabarovsk (A), Irkutsk (B) and Novosibirsk (D) are stations along the route, not its terminal.
Key point: Chita is an important agro-centre and Irkutsk a fur centre on this route.

questions.sub_topic: Chief exports on the Trans-Canadian route

Question: The Trans-Canadian Railway links Canada's industrial east with the Prairie wheat belt and the northern forests. According to NCERT, which are the important exports carried on this route?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Wheat and meat
Why: NCERT states that wheat and meat are the important exports on the Trans-Canadian route, coming from the Prairie wheat belt and its livestock farms.
Why not the others: Coal and iron ore (A), cotton and tobacco (C) and rubber (D) are not NCERT's export items for this route; rubber is a tropical crop.
Key point: The Trans-Canadian line runs from Halifax in the east to Vancouver in the west.

Question: Which two cities are linked by the Union and Pacific Railway, which crosses the USA from the Atlantic coast to the Pacific coast?
options: D) New York and San Francisco
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) New York and San Francisco
Why: NCERT notes that the Union and Pacific Railway connects New York on the Atlantic coast with San Francisco on the Pacific coast, passing through Cleveland, Chicago, Omaha, Evans, Ogden and Sacramento.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the terminals of this railway; Chicago is a station along it.
Key point: Ores, grain, paper, chemicals and machinery are its main exports.

Question: The Australian Trans-Continental Railway runs across the southern part of the continent from the west coast to the east coast. Which two cities does it link?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Perth and Sydney
Why: NCERT notes that the Australian Trans-Continental Railway runs from Perth on the west coast to Sydney on the east coast, through Kalgoorlie, Broken Hill and Port Augusta.
Why not the others: (B) runs north–south; (C) lies along the east coast; (D) runs along the west and north.
Key point: Another major line in Australia runs north–south, from Adelaide to Alice Springs.

Question: Which of the following statements about the Orient Express is correct, according to NCERT?
options: A) It runs from Moscow to Vladivostok across Siberia, carrying mainly furs and timber
B) It links Halifax with Vancouver, passing through the wheat belt of the Prairies
C) It runs from Paris to Istanbul and cut the London–Istanbul journey to about 96 hours
D) It links Perth with Sydney, passing through Kalgoorlie, Broken Hill and Port Augusta
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) It runs from Paris to Istanbul and cut the London–Istanbul journey to about 96 hours
Why: NCERT notes that the Orient Express runs from Paris to Istanbul, passing through Strasbourg, Munich, Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade; it reduced the journey from London to Istanbul to 96 hours, compared with 10 days by sea.
Why not the others: (A) describes part of the Trans-Siberian route; (B) is the Trans-Canadian; (D) is the Australian Trans-Continental.
Key point: Cheese, bacon, oats, wine, fruits and machinery are carried on the Orient Express route.
